items.question: What practice must follow worship of this circle to activate its power?
premises: Meditation is then applied to it.
The practice continues for a duration.
items.inference: Sustained meditation after worship activates the circle's efficacy.
items.plain_english: Having worshipped this circle, one applies meditation to it for as long as one continues the practice.

items.question: What kinds of languages become perceptible through this meditative practice?
items.inference: The practice grants perception of diverse languages, both familiar and unfamiliar.
items.plain_english: Indeed, languages of various forms, both unheard and heard, become perceptible.

items.question: How and where are these diverse languages heard by the practitioner?
premises: The practitioner hears by oneself and to oneself.
The hearing takes place within oneself.
items.inference: The languages are heard inwardly and spontaneously by the practitioner alone.
uncertainties: The precise syntactic roles of the repeated forms of ātman are ambiguous.
items.plain_english: Indeed, they are heard spontaneously by oneself, to oneself, and within oneself.

items.question: What bodily transformation results from the successful practice described above?
premises: The practitioner becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair.
The practitioner resembles the god of love.
The resemblance is that of a second Kāma.
items.inference: The practice confers youthful beauty comparable to a second god of love.
items.plain_english: Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, one becomes like a second god of love.

items.question: What effect on speech can be produced by destroying the force of wind and related elements?
premises: The force of wind and so forth is destroyed.
The person remains like a mute.
items.inference: Destroying the force of wind and related elements renders a person mute.
uncertainties: Whether vāyvādeḥ refers to the wind element, wind deities, or related forces is unclear.
items.plain_english: By destroying the force of wind and so forth through speech, he indeed remains standing like a mute.

items.question: What supreme power is attributed to the seventh circle addressed to the goddess?
premises: It is addressed to the goddess.
Its function is to paralyze armies.
items.inference: The seventh circle possesses the supreme power to paralyze armies.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, the seventh circle is supreme and causes the paralysis of armies.

items.question: What perceptual ability arises for one devoted to worship and meditation on that circle?
premises: The practitioner is devoted to worship and meditation.
items.inference: Devotion to worship and meditation on that circle grants distant vision.
items.plain_english: Indeed, for one devoted to worship and meditation on that circle, vision arises even from afar.

items.question: What further magical operations become possible through this circle's power?
items.inference: The circle enables killing, uprooting, paralyzing, deluding, and related operations.
items.plain_english: O fortunate one, O beloved, killing, uprooting, paralyzing, deluding, and such acts become possible.

items.question: What knowledge is required for success in these practices to be attained?
premises: The method of eight times eight must be known.
items.inference: Knowledge of the eight-times-eight method is necessary for success.
uncertainties: The exact content of the eight-times-eight method is not specified.
items.plain_english: Indeed, having known the method of the eight times eight, one succeeds; not otherwise.

items.question: How should the certainty of this teaching be properly ascertained by the listener?
premises: The teaching is declared without doubt.
items.inference: The teaching is certain and must be ascertained through devotion and reasoning.
items.plain_english: Indeed, I have declared this without doubt; ascertain it with devotion and reasoning.

items.question: Which chapter concludes the section that emerged from Candradvīpa?
items.inference: The eighth chapter concludes the section emerged from Candradvīpa.
uncertainties: The exact referent of candradvīpavinirgate may be a text or tradition.
items.plain_english: This is the eighth chapter in that which emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: What new topic will the speaker now explain to the beloved listener?
premises: The speaker intends to tell something.
The topic is the arrangement of yoginī rows.
items.inference: The speaker will now explain the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs.
items.plain_english: O beloved, I shall tell you the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs.

items.question: What collective domain encompasses all earth-moving and sky-moving yoginīs?
premises: They belong to a complete field-group.
items.inference: All earth-moving and sky-moving yoginīs together constitute the complete field-group.
uncertainties: The precise meaning of sarvakṣetrakam as a technical term is uncertain.
items.plain_english: This is the complete field-group of all earth-moving and all sky-moving yoginīs.

items.question: Which categories of yoginīs are included within this comprehensive arrangement?
items.inference: The arrangement includes innate, family-born, and door-guardian yoginīs.
items.plain_english: All the innate ones, all the family-born ones, and all the door-guardians are included.

items.question: Why has the supreme secret among all secrets now been revealed?
premises: It is the supreme secret among secrets.
The revelation is due to the listener's devotion.
items.inference: The supreme secret is revealed because of the listener's devotion.
items.plain_english: The supreme secret of secrets has been revealed because of your devotion.

items.question: What instruction does the speaker now wish to hear from the gurus?
premises: The speaker expresses a present wish.
The wish is to hear from the gurus.
The topic is the worship of the siddhas.
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear about the worship of the siddhas from the gurus.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear from the gurus about the worship of the siddhas.

items.question: To whom should the arrangement of the two syllables be transmitted?
premises: There is an arrangement of two syllables.
items.inference: The two-syllable arrangement should be given to others as prescribed.
uncertainties: The referent of anyanteṣu is unclear in this context.
items.plain_english: One should give the arrangement of the two syllables to others.

items.question: What claim is made about the uniqueness of this knowledge in the future?
premises: This knowledge is the standard of comparison.
No equal knowledge will arise again.
items.inference: No knowledge equal to this will ever exist in the future.
items.plain_english: There is no knowledge equal to this, nor will there ever be again.

items.question: What does the speaker promise to explain next to the beautiful-eyed listener?
premises: The speaker addresses the listener directly.
The topic is the method of their names.
items.inference: The speaker will explain the method of their names to the listener.
uncertainties: The referent of teṣāṃ is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: O beautiful-eyed one, listen; I shall speak the method of their names.

items.question: Who are identified as the independent impellers of the lineage across the four ages?
premises: The term four ages is invoked.
They are impellers of the lineage.
items.inference: The independent impellers of the lineage are identified in relation to the four ages.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of caturyuga iti is somewhat compressed.
items.plain_english: O Lord, thus are the independent impellers of the lineage of the four ages.

items.question: What magnitude and origin are attributed to this Kaula teaching?
items.inference: This supremely arisen Kaula teaching has a measure of ten crores.
uncertainties: The unit or referent of the measure of ten crores is unspecified.
items.plain_english: Indeed, this Kaula teaching, supremely arisen, is ten crores in measure.

items.question: By whose agency and will does the yoginī named Icchā extend up to māyā?
premises: The siddhas are involved as agents.
The action occurs by supreme will up to māyā.
items.inference: The yoginī Icchā, through the siddhas and by supreme will, extends up to māyā.
uncertainties: The main verb is implicit, making the exact action unclear.
items.plain_english: The yoginī named Icchā, by the siddhas and by supreme will, extends up to māyā.

items.question: Who transmitted the teaching concerning the mothers to the goddess?
premises: The sky-movers were the agents of transmission.
items.inference: The sky-movers told the teaching concerning the mothers.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, O beloved, it was told again to the mothers by the sky-movers.

items.question: Who transmitted the teaching to the earth-moving yoginīs described as good eaters?
premises: The recipients are the earth-moving yoginīs.
They are described as good eaters.
items.inference: An earth-mover transmitted the teaching to the earth-moving yoginīs who are good eaters.
uncertainties: The form bhūcarī is taken as instrumental singular but could be ambiguous.
items.plain_english: O beloved, it was told to the earth-moving yoginīs, the good eaters, by an earth-mover.
